scope: Bring up the RESMP calibrated Qwen IQ2_XS/Q2_0 artifact on B550, repair the split-GGUF pack metadata, build the missing Q2_0 MTP drafter, and collect first single- versus two-GPU execution and warm short-generation observations.

gpu_occupancy.before: 2026-10-19T13:12:37Z: both GPUs 0 percent compute; only two cuda_embed_server replicas resident (GPU0 2160 MiB, GPU1 5120 MiB).
gpu_occupancy.during_first_gpu0_run: A transient unrelated embedding burst took both GPUs to 92 and 100 percent; that timing observation is excluded as a control.
gpu_occupancy.after: 2026-10-19 after model shutdown: both GPUs idle; only the same embedding replicas remain resident (GPU0 3210 MiB, GPU1 5120 MiB). No service was stopped or restarted.

split_pack_repair.problem_1: The direct one-shot command used the historical generate subcommand, but this pinned engine uses a verbless direct CLI.
split_pack_repair.problem_2: The published unsharded pack offsets do not match the split GGUF: layer 0 gate experts differ by exactly 56000 bytes.
split_pack_repair.problem_3: The PLE tensor is in shard 1, not shard 2.
split_pack_repair.command: STRATA_GGUF_PY=/home/kearm/strata-llamacpp-3cf0325/gguf-py uv run --with numpy --with pyyaml --with regex python tools/iq_pack.py --gguf <shard1> --out pack-split --compat-bf16
split_pack_repair.output: native_experts v4; layer 13 gate/up/down use per-role shard fields; dense.bin and all tokenizer files byte-identical to the original pack

gpu0_first.nonclaim: Overlapped an unrelated 92/100 percent embedding burst; execution proof only, not a clean timing control.

gpu1.identity: The 25.0 GB/s PCIe probe confirms physical GPU1/0000:08:00.0; engine logs call the remapped device CUDA0.

one_shot_execution.nondeterminism: With fixed prompt, engine, profile, cache slots, and greedy sampling, B550 produced tokens 157, 487, and 220 across these runs. One-token agreement with Strix token 157 is therefore not a cross-host correctness gate.

server_benchmarks.workload: Three identical local OpenAI chat requests; prompt 25 tokens, max 128, greedy, reasoning effort none; first request discarded as warm-up.

two_gpu_auto_mtp_pipeline_windows_2.observation: Directionally about 6 percent faster warm decode but fewer resident experts and lower acceptance; only two measured runs per arm.

server_benchmarks.comparison: Two-GPU warm decode is about 1.9x GPU1 alone and 2.4x GPU0 alone on this workload. GPU1 is the better single card despite fewer slots because its CPU-root Gen4 x16 link reduces miss cost.

non_claims: These are short warm-generation observations, not medians from the required five or more interleaved runs per arm.
The first no-MTP two-GPU one-token 38.5 tok/s probe is a load probe, not a matched throughput baseline.
One-token argmax changes across B550 runs, so one-token parity does not prove correctness or quality.
No long-prompt, 128K-context, multi-client, batch, helper-expert, manual split, adapt-async, fused-prefill, or acceptance-quality benchmark is claimed.
The MTP Q2_0 drafter is exercised on one short coding prompt only; acceptance on other domains and longer generations is unmeasured.
The task-owned servers were stopped; the two unrelated cuda_embed_server replicas remain resident and untouched.
